criteria.name: title_is_noun_phrase
criteria.definition: Title reads as a noun phrase, not a sentence or question. Examples that pass: 'Project-create flow QA on staging', 'Login regression repro'. Examples that fail: 'I tested the project-create flow', 'Did the login work?'

criteria.name: description_is_spoken_intro
criteria.definition: Description reads aloud as the first thing a presenter would say. No greeting, no 'welcome', no 'today we'll'. Direct, present-tense, lands the spine in 1-2 sentences.

criteria.name: no_banned_phrases
criteria.definition: None of the banned phrases appear in title, description, captions, or summary. Case-insensitive substring match.

criteria.name: voice_consistency
criteria.definition: One voice runs through intro, every caption, and outro. Not three voices stitched together.

criteria.name: captions_land_a_point
criteria.definition: Each caption lands on the non-obvious detail, not the literal screen content. Captions that enumerate visible elements ('Page shows hero, nav, footer') fail. Captions that name what is interesting or surprising about that state pass.

criteria.name: reads_as_speech_not_prose
criteria.definition: Read the description, every caption, and the summary aloud. They must sound like a real video transcript -- someone talking on camera -- not written prose. Spoken text uses fragments, varied sentence length, and one idea per line. Flag written-prose tells: enumerations ('X has A, B, and C'), clauses stacked with 'and'/'which' into one long sentence, throat-clearing ('it is worth noting that'), and tidy evenly-balanced sentences that read like documentation. A clip can hit every voice marker and still fail this if it reads like a blog post.

criteria.name: run_type_match
criteria.definition: The chosen run_type matches the trigger phrasing of the user_prompt. demo=showcase/walk through/show off. qa=QA/smoke/verify/regression. guide=how-to/explain/compare/investigate. bug=repro/reproduce/bug/broken.

demo.voice_definition: Someone who just shipped a thing and hit record on Loom to show you. First-person ('I'll show you', 'we just shipped'). Conversational, contractions throughout. Acknowledges the viewer ('watch this', 'you can see'). Mild editorial reactions allowed ('which I really like', 'took us a few iterations'). NOT marketing copy, NOT design-critic tightness. The vibe to match: a friend recording a quick walkthrough of something they're proud of.

extra_criteria.name: loom_voice_tells
extra_criteria.definition: Captions and description should contain at least 2-3 Loom-style markers across the clip: first-person ('I/we/our'), direct address ('you/watch/notice'), contractions ('won't', 'doesn't', 'that's'), or mild editorial ('really nice', 'pretty clean', 'took some iteration'). A clip with zero of these reads as Linear marketing copy and fails this criterion. Don't require ALL slides to use them — natural conversation rhythm matters more than checking every caption.

extra_criteria.name: no_meta_framing
extra_criteria.definition: Description does not open with meta-framing like 'A 30-second look at...', 'Here's a quick walkthrough of...', or 'Today I'll be showing you...'. The first words should land directly on what the viewer is about to see, not on what kind of clip this is.

extra_criteria.name: title_drops_engineer_frame
extra_criteria.definition: Demo title is product-y, not engineer-y. 'New signup flow', 'Signup, redesigned', 'Walking through the new signup' all pass. 'Signup flow on staging', 'Signup QA results', or anything mentioning environments/branches/tickets fails — those leak the engineering frame into a demo title.

qa.voice_definition: Someone running a checklist out loud for another engineer. Each slide ends with a verdict: worked / passed / broken / clean. Brisk, blunt, factual. NO Loom warmth here — qa voice rewards tightness, not friendliness. Editorial asides ('which I really like') are wrong register for qa.

extra_criteria.name: every_slide_has_verdict
extra_criteria.definition: Each caption ends with or contains a clear verdict (worked / passed / failed / broken / clean / good / bad / correct). Failures must be called out explicitly with what failed.

extra_criteria.name: summary_has_passfail_counts
extra_criteria.definition: Summary names pass/fail counts (e.g. '5/5 passed') or the specific bugs found with slide references.

guide.voice_definition: Friendly product-explainer YouTube channel (Fireship, Theo, Web Dev Simplified vibe). Second-person ('you'll notice', 'watch what happens'). Stakes-aware ('most signup flows still get this wrong'). Editorial asides allowed ('small thing, big difference'). Specifics over generalities. NOT clinical analyst — there should be warmth.

extra_criteria.name: youtuber_voice_tells
extra_criteria.definition: Captions and description should contain at least 2-3 YouTuber-style markers across the clip: second-person address ('you/watch/notice/you'll'), stakes-aware contrast ('most X get this wrong', 'unlike most...'), or editorial asides ('small thing big difference', 'honestly the move'). A clip with zero of these reads as a clinical research report and fails. Don't require EVERY slide to use them.

extra_criteria.name: lands_a_takeaway
extra_criteria.definition: The clip lands one specific conclusion, not multiple loose observations. The final caption or summary names the takeaway.

extra_criteria.name: specifics_over_generalities
extra_criteria.definition: Captions name concrete numbers, geographies, ISPs, model names, time windows — not vague gestures at 'the data' or 'the trend'.

bug.voice_definition: Senior engineer narrating a repro to another senior engineer. No setup, no closure. Just facts. Past-tense is fine because you're recapping.

extra_criteria.name: establish_reproduce_prove
extra_criteria.definition: The captions follow establish-state -> reproduce -> prove. Not all three slides need be present but the arc must read as a repro, not a tour.

extra_criteria.name: summary_states_outcome
extra_criteria.definition: Summary states the bug outcome with a slide reference. 'Bug confirmed at slide 2. /api/auth/signup returns 503 instead of either succeeding or rate-limit-error.' is the target shape.
